EDUMIND COLLEGE OF ENGINEERING & TECHNOLOGY
ACADEMIC CALENDAR, CURRICULUM SCHEME & TIMETABLE REGULATIONS
Document Code: ECET-ACAD-CAL-2026

1. ACADEMIC CALENDAR OVERVIEW
1.1 The academic year comprises two semesters: Odd Semester (July to December) and Even Semester (January to June).
1.2 Each semester consists of a minimum of 90 instructional days (15 teaching weeks) excluding examination and preparation breaks.

1.3 Important Dates for the Current Academic Year:
    - Odd Semester Commencement: July 15th
    - Continuous Assessment Test-1 (CAT-1): September 10th to 16th
    - Mid-Semester Technical Fest & Cultural Days: October 3rd to 5th
    - Continuous Assessment Test-2 (CAT-2): November 4th to 10th
    - Practical & Oral Examination Sessions: November 20th to 28th
    - End-Semester Theory Examinations: December 2nd to December 22nd
    - Semester Vacation: December 23rd to January 9th
    - Even Semester Classes Begin: January 10th

2.

CHOICE-BASED CREDIT SYSTEM (CBCS) & COURSE REGISTRATION
2.1 B.Tech degree completion requires a cumulative earning of 160 academic credits distributed across:
    - Basic Science Courses (BSC): 24 Credits
    - Engineering Science Courses (ESC): 22 Credits
    - Professional Core Courses (PCC): 64 Credits
    - Professional Elective Courses (PEC): 18 Credits
    - Open Elective Courses (OEC): 12 Credits
    - Humanities & Social Sciences (HSMC): 12 Credits
    - Capstone Project Work & Internship: 16 Credits
2.2 Mandatory Course Registration takes place online in the first week of each semester.

A student may register for a maximum of 28 credits per semester. 2.3 Adding or dropping elective courses is allowed within 10 instructional days of semester start with Academic Mentor recommendation. 2.4 Online MOOC credits: Up to 8 credits can be earned via approved NPTEL / SWAYAM 12-week certification courses with prior Dean approval. 3.

3. MASTER TIMETABLE & WORKING HOURS
3.1 Instructional hours operate from 9:00 AM to 4:45 PM, Monday through Friday, divided into 7 lecture periods of 50 minutes each and a 55-minute lunch break (12:40 PM - 1:35 PM). 3.2 Laboratory sessions are conducted in consecutive 2-hour practical slots for designated batches of 20 students.

3.3 Saturday schedules are designated for co-curricular clubs, remedial tutorial sessions, NSS/sports activities, and student mentor meetings. 3.4 Official notifications, class schedules, and room allocations are published on the department notice boards and EduMind Student Mobile App.

EDUMIND COLLEGE OF ENGINEERING & TECHNOLOGY
OFFICIAL REGULATION: ATTENDANCE POLICY AND DETENTION RULES
Document Code: ECET-REG-ATT-2026-v2

1.

MINIMUM ATTENDANCE REQUIREMENT
1.1 Every student is required to maintain a minimum attendance of 75% in aggregate across all registered courses (theory, laboratory, tutorials, and project work) in each semester to be eligible to appear for the end-semester examinations.

1.2 For laboratory courses and practical workshops, a strict minimum of 80% physical attendance is mandatory due to hands-on equipment and safety compliance. 1.3 Daily attendance is recorded electronically on the EduMind Student ERP portal at the conclusion of every lecture period and synced daily at 6:00 PM. 2.

2. CONDONATION OF SHORTAGE OF ATTENDANCE
2.1 Condonation of attendance shortage between 65% and 74% may be granted by the College Academic Committee and the Principal only on genuine medical grounds or approved representation in university-level sports, NCC, NSS, or collegiate technical events.

2.2 For medical condonation, students must submit a formal medical leave application along with a registered medical practitioner's certificate and hospital discharge summary to the Head of the Department (HOD) within three working days of resuming classes. 2.3 An administrative condonation processing fee of Rs. 500 per subject is applicable for approved condonations.

500 per subject is applicable for approved condonations. 2.4 Attendance below 65% shall NOT be condoned under any circumstances, including severe medical illness. 3. DETENTION AND DEBARMENT PROCEDURE
3.1 Students whose overall attendance remains below 75% (or 65% with approved condonation) shall be officially classified as 'Detained' for that academic semester.

3.2 Detained students are debarred from appearing in the regular end-semester theory and practical examinations. 3.3 A detained student will receive an 'F' (Fail) grade and must re-register for the entire semester courses in the subsequent academic year by paying the requisite semester re-admission tuition fees.

3.4 The provisional detention warning list is published by each department on the 1st of every month, and the final detention list is displayed seven days prior to the commencement of end-semester examinations. 4.

4. ATTENDANCE GRIEVANCE REDRESSAL
4.1 Any discrepancy in recorded attendance must be brought to the notice of the concerned course instructor and Academic Coordinator within 48 hours of posting on the ERP. 4.2 Unresolved disputes may be escalated in writing to the Student Attendance Grievance Redressal Committee headed by the Dean of Academic Affairs.

EDUMIND COLLEGE OF ENGINEERING & TECHNOLOGY
OFFICIAL REGULATION: EXAMINATION RULES, EVALUATION & REVALUATION GUIDELINES
Document Code: ECET-EXAM-REG-2026

1. EXAMINATION STRUCTURE AND ELIGIBILITY
1.1 The college conducts two In-Semester Continuous Assessment Tests (CAT-1 and CAT-2) carrying 20% weightage each, and one Comprehensive End-Semester Examination (ESE) carrying 60% weightage.

1.2 To qualify for appearing in the End-Semester Examination, a candidate must have:
    a) Maintained minimum 75% attendance in theory and 80% in laboratories. b) Cleared all tuition, laboratory, and library dues. c) Submitted all term-work assignments, mini-projects, and laboratory records certified by the faculty.

1.3 The morning session examination operates from 9:30 AM to 12:30 PM, and the afternoon session operates from 2:00 PM to 5:00 PM. Candidates must report at least 30 minutes before exam commencement. 2.

2. EXAMINATION REGISTRATION AND HALL TICKETS
2.1 All eligible students must register online via the Examination Portal (exams.edumind.ac.in) for regular and backlog subjects at least 21 days before the scheduled exam date. 2.2 The regular examination registration fee is Rs. 1,500 per semester. Late registration with penalty of Rs. 500 is permitted up to 7 days after the regular deadline.

500 is permitted up to 7 days after the regular deadline. 2.3 Hall Tickets / Admit Cards can be downloaded 5 days prior to exams after HOD online endorsement. 2.4 Carrying the printed Hall Ticket and valid College Identity Card inside the examination hall is strictly compulsory. Electronic gadgets, smartwatches, and programmable calculators are strictly prohibited. 3.

3. PASSING CRITERIA AND GRADING SYSTEM
3.1 A student must secure a minimum of 40% marks in the End-Semester Examination and an aggregate of 45% (CAT + ESE) to obtain a passing grade in each subject.

3.2 Absolute 10-point Letter Grading Scale:
    - O (Outstanding): 90% and above (Grade Point: 10)
    - A+ (Excellent): 80% to 89% (Grade Point: 9)
    - A (Very Good): 70% to 79% (Grade Point: 8)
    - B+ (Good): 60% to 69% (Grade Point: 7)
    - B (Above Average): 50% to 59% (Grade Point: 6)
    - C (Pass): 45% to 49% (Grade Point: 5)
    - F (Fail): Below 45% (Grade Point: 0)
3.3 Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA) is computed as the weighted credit average of all semesters completed.

4. REVALUATION, RE-TOTALING AND PHOTOCOPY OF SCRIPTS
4.1 Students dissatisfied with their results may apply for Photocopy of Answer Scripts within 7 days of result declaration by paying Rs. 300 per subject. 4.2 Revaluation and Re-totaling applications must be submitted within 10 days of receiving the photocopy, accompanied by a fee of Rs. 700 per subject.

700 per subject. 4.3 If revaluation results in a mark increase greater than 10% of maximum marks, the revised score replaces the original score, and 50% of the revaluation fee is refunded to the student. 4.4 Revaluation results are published within 25 working days from the application deadline.

EDUMIND COLLEGE OF ENGINEERING & TECHNOLOGY
OFFICIAL REGULATION: TUITION FEES, HOSTEL DUES & SCHOLARSHIP SCHEMES
Document Code: ECET-FIN-SCH-2026

1. ANNUAL TUITION AND ACADEMIC FEES
1.1 The annual tuition fee for B.Tech Undergraduate engineering programs is Rs. 1,45,000 per academic year, payable in two equal semester installments. 1.2 Breakdown of Semester Fees:
    - Tuition Fee: Rs.

1.2 Breakdown of Semester Fees:
    - Tuition Fee: Rs. 60,000 per semester
    - Development and Infrastructure Fee: Rs. 10,000 per semester
    - Laboratory and Computer Network Fee: Rs. 5,000 per semester
    - Library & Digital Resources Subscription: Rs. 2,500 per semester
    - Student Gymkhana, Sports & Cultural Fee: Rs.

2,500 per semester
    - Refundable Caution Deposit (One-time at admission): Rs. 10,000
1.3 All fees must be paid online via net banking, UPI, or debit/credit card through the EduMind ERP Fee Gateway. Cash payments are not accepted. 2. FEE PAYMENT DEADLINES AND PENALTIES
2.1 Odd Semester tuition fee must be cleared on or before July 31st.

2.2 Even Semester tuition fee must be cleared on or before December 31st. 2.3 A late payment penalty of Rs. 100 per day is levied for payments received between 1 and 15 days past deadline. 2.4 Accounts showing dues past 30 days will experience temporary ERP account suspension and exam hall ticket withholding.

2.5 Fee payment in installments requires prior written approval from the Registrar and Finance Officer on financial hardship demonstration. 3. HOSTEL AND MESS FEES
3.1 Triple-occupancy room with attached washroom: Rs. 45,000 per semester. 3.2 Double-occupancy AC room: Rs. 65,000 per semester. 3.3 Annual refundable hostel caution deposit: Rs. 8,000. 3.4 Mandatory cooperative mess subscription: Rs.

8,000. 3.4 Mandatory cooperative mess subscription: Rs. 24,000 per semester (4 meals daily, vegetarian and non-vegetarian options). 4. SCHOLARSHIP SCHEMES AND TUITION CONCESSIONS
4.1 EduMind Merit Scholarship: 50% tuition waiver awarded to students securing top 5 ranks in their department with CGPA >= 9.2.

4.2 Economically Weaker Section (EWS) Assistance: Up to 40% tuition concession for students with verified annual family income below Rs. 4,00,000. 4.3 Government Scholarships: The college nodal scholarship cell facilitates Maharashtra Post-Matric Scholarship (MahaDBT), Central Sector Scholarship, and AICTE Pragati Scholarship for girl students.
4.4 Sports Excellence Award: Full tuition fee waiver for students representing the state or country in recognized national/international sporting championships.

EDUMIND COLLEGE OF ENGINEERING & TECHNOLOGY
CENTRAL LIBRARY & INFORMATION RESOURCE CENTRE: USER MANUAL
Document Code: ECET-LIB-MAN-2026

1. GENERAL TIMINGS AND MEMBERSHIP
1.1 The Central Library operates from 8:00 AM to 9:00 PM on all working days (Monday through Saturday).

1.2 During mid-term and end-semester examination periods, the 24x7 Reading Hall remains open overnight for registered students. 1.3 All bona fide students, faculty, and research scholars are automatically enrolled as library members upon issuance of their Barcoded Smart Identity Card. 2.

2. CIRCULATION AND BORROWING PRIVILEGES
2.1 Undergraduate (B.Tech) Students: May borrow up to 4 books simultaneously for a borrowing period of 14 calendar days. 2.2 Postgraduate (M.Tech) & Research Scholars: May borrow up to 6 books for a duration of 28 calendar days. 2.3 Book renewals can be executed twice online via the Web-OPAC system, provided no reservation hold exists from another user.

2.4 Overdue Fine Structure:
    - Days 1 to 7 overdue: Rs. 5 per book per day. - Beyond 7 days overdue: Rs. 15 per book per day. 2.5 In case of lost or irreparably damaged books, the borrower must replace the book with the latest edition or pay three times the current catalogue market price plus Rs. 100 processing surcharge. 3.

100 processing surcharge. 3. DIGITAL LIBRARY & E-RESOURCES
3.1 The Digital Library section houses 60 high-performance computer terminals equipped with high-speed internet and research tools.

3.2 Subscribed Online Databases & Electronic Journals:
    - IEEE Xplore Digital Library (Full-text access to all conferences and journals)
    - ACM Digital Library & SpringerLink Nature Journals
    - ScienceDirect (Elsevier) & ASCE / ASME Digital Collections
    - NPTEL video lecture repositories and Swayam local cache servers
3.3 RemoteXs Off-Campus Remote Access: Students can access digital databases from outside the campus using institutional email SSO credentials at elibrary.edumind.ac.in.

3.4 Anti-Plagiarism Screening: The library provides Turnitin and Urkund originality similarity verification for student project reports, thesis dissertations, and technical papers. A similarity index below 15% is mandatory for thesis submission. 4. CODE OF CONDUCT
4.1 Silence must be strictly observed in reading halls. Mobile phone usage in voice mode is strictly banned inside library premises.

4.2 Bags, personal books, and umbrellas must be deposited at the property counter before entering. 4.3 Library 'No-Dues Clearance' certificate is mandatory for final semester graduation and issuance of degree transcripts.

EDUMIND COLLEGE OF ENGINEERING & TECHNOLOGY
TRAINING & PLACEMENT CELL (T&P) GUIDELINES & RECRUITMENT POLICY
Document Code: ECET-TNP-POL-2026

1. PLACEMENT ELIGIBILITY & REGISTRATION
1.1 All final-year students seeking campus recruitment assistance must register with the T&P Portal (placement.edumind.ac.in) by July 15th with verified academic credentials.

1.2 Minimum Academic Eligibility:
    - Tier-1 Product Companies (CTC > 12 LPA): Minimum CGPA 8.0 without any live or past standing backlogs. - Tier-2 Core and IT Service Companies (CTC 6 to 12 LPA): Minimum CGPA 7.0 with maximum 1 standing backlog. - Mass Recruiters / Consultancies (CTC 3.5 to 6 LPA): Minimum CGPA 6.0 with maximum 2 allowed backlogs.
1.3 Attendance in all pre-placement training modules (quantitative aptitude, logical reasoning, verbal communication, DSA coding bootcamps, and mock interviews) must be at least 85%. 2.

2. CAMPUS RECRUITMENT POLICY (ONE STUDENT - ONE OFFER)
2.1 To ensure equitable opportunities, EduMind follows a modified 'One Student, One Job Offer' policy:
    - Once a student receives an offer in Tier-3 category (< 6 LPA), they are permitted to compete only for Tier-1 'Dream' companies offering 2x of their current offer.

- An offer from a Tier-1 Dream company (> 12 LPA) is considered final, and the candidate is immediately de-registered from all further placement drives. 2.2 Accepting an on-campus placement offer requires signing the Letter of Intent (LOI) within 48 hours. Failing to honor an accepted offer leads to permanent debarment from campus recruitment services. 3.

3. INTERNSHIP GUIDELINES & CREDITS
3.1 Eighth-semester students may undertake full-time 6-month industry internships with stipend >= Rs. 20,000 per month, subject to departmental approval and No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the T&P Cell.

3.2 A 6-month industry internship carries 12 academic credits in lieu of elective coursework and capstone project-2, evaluated via monthly faculty reviews and joint company mentor appraisal. 4. RECRUITMENT STATISTICS HIGHLIGHTS
4.1 Over 140 premier technology companies participate in campus placements annually, including Google, Microsoft, Amazon, TCS, Infosys, Cognizant, L&T, and Tata Motors.

4.2 Highest international package offered: Rs. 44.5 LPA. Highest domestic package: Rs. 32 LPA. Average engineering package across all branches: Rs. 7.8 LPA. 4.3 T&P Cell contact: placement@edumind.ac.in, Office Room #204, Administrative Block.
